channel.title: Buick recalls — Car Recall Tracker
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Buick and Chevrolet Rearview Camera May Show Blank Image
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Buick Envista, Buick Encore GX, Chevrolet Trailblazer, and Chevrolet Trax vehicles because the rearview camera screen may display a distorted or blank image instead of showing what's behind the vehicle clearly.

item.title: Buick Envision Missing Tire Information Label
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Buick Envision vehicles because they are missing a label that lists the correct tire size, correct tire pressure, and vehicle loading information. Because this label is missing, that tire and loading information is not available to the owner where it is supposed to be. As a result, these vehicles do not meet the federal safety standard that covers tire and rim selection information for vehicles.

item.title: Buick, Chevrolet Instrument Panel May Go Blank
item.description: A software problem can cause the instrument panel display to intermittently go blank. This can happen either right when the vehicle is started or at any point while it is being driven. When the screen goes blank, it stops showing information that is normally displayed there, such as the vehicle's speed and any warning lights that would otherwise be lit. As a result, the driver may not be able to see that information for as long as the screen stays blank.

item.title: GM Vehicles Daytime Running Lights Stay On
item.description: In certain Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC vehicles, the daytime running lights may not turn off when the headlights are switched on. This can create glare and reduce visibility for other drivers.

item.title: Buick Regal Power Brake Assist Failure Risk
item.description: Certain Buick Regal vehicles may lose power brake assist if there is a vacuum-power brake assist failure. A software error in the brake control module can cause this loss of assist. Without power assist, it takes more distance to bring the vehicle to a stop, which increases the risk of a crash. Because of this issue, these vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard for brake systems.

item.title: Buick Enclave, Chevy Traverse Side Air Bag Wiring
item.description: On certain Chevrolet Traverse and Buick Enclave vehicles, the electrical connector for the wiring harness leading to the roof rail (side curtain) air bag may have terminals that don't fit together correctly. If the connection isn't right, the roof rail air bag on that side of the vehicle may not deploy the way it's supposed to in a crash.

item.title: Chevrolet Traverse and Buick Enclave got wrong airbag software
item.description: GM is recalling certain Chevrolet Traverse and Buick Enclave vehicles. When these vehicles were serviced at a dealership, some of them may have been given incorrect software settings for the air bag system. Because the settings are wrong, the front air bags may not work the way they are meant to. A dealer needs to load the correct air bag software onto the vehicle, and there is no charge for that work.

item.title: GM vehicles' airbag warning light works inconsistently
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet and GMC vehicles. The module that passes messages between vehicle systems does not correctly handle a loss of communication with the airbag sensing module. As a result, the airbag warning light on the dashboard turns on inconsistently. A dealer can update that module's software, or the update can be sent to the vehicle over the air, free of charge. GM mailed owner notification letters on July 1, 2021.

item.title: Buick Encore GX and Chevrolet Trailblazer emergency jack can break
item.description: General Motors is recalling certain Buick Encore GX and Chevrolet Trailblazer vehicles because of a problem with the emergency jack that comes with the vehicle, the tool that lifts the vehicle off the ground. If the jack is not placed the way the owner's manual describes, it can break while it is holding the vehicle up. Dealers will replace the jack with a new one at no cost to the owner.

item.title: GM Vehicles Recalled for Over-Cured Tire Failure Risk
item.description: The tires on these vehicles were left in the curing process for too long during manufacturing. Tires that are cured too long can develop a break in the sidewall, which can cause sudden air loss, or the tire's belt edge can separate, causing the tread or belt to come apart. Either problem can cause the driver to lose control of the vehicle.

item.title: GM trucks and SUVs recalled for overcured tires
item.description: This recall covers certain Buick Enclave, Cadillac XT5, GMC Acadia, and Chevrolet Traverse vehicles, along with certain Chevrolet Silverado 1500 and GMC Sierra 1500 trucks. These vehicles may have been built with Continental tires that were overcured during manufacturing.

item.title: GM transmission bolts missing, leak and fire risk
item.description: On certain GM vehicles, the endcap on the start/stop transmission accumulator may be missing bolts. This can let transmission fluid leak out. Over time, the leak can get bad enough that the vehicle loses the ability to move forward. If the leaking fluid comes into contact with something that can ignite it, it could catch fire.

item.title: GM SUVs' Fuel Pump Blockage Can Stall Engine
item.description: In some of these vehicles, a leftover piece of plastic from manufacturing may be stuck in the fuel pump's nozzle. This can block the nozzle and keep enough fuel from reaching the engine. When that happens, the engine may not get the fuel it needs to keep running. GM will have dealers replace the fuel pump module to fix the problem, at no cost to owners.

item.title: Chevrolet, Cadillac, Buick Models Lose Brake Assist
item.description: Contamination at a sensor connection in the electronic brake boost system may interrupt communication between the sensor and the brake booster. This affects certain Chevrolet Corvette and Trailblazer, Cadillac CT4, CT5 and XT4, and Buick Encore GX vehicles. If that happens, the power assist that helps you brake could be lost, meaning you would need much more pedal force to slow or stop the vehicle. Dealers will replace the electronic brake boost module, free of charge.

item.title: Buick Encore and Chevy Trailblazer Seat Bolts Missing
item.description: On some vehicles, one or both front seats may be missing the bolts that attach the back of the seat to the vehicle. Without these attachment bolts, a seat with someone sitting in it can shift or move out of position if the vehicle is in a crash, which increases the risk that the occupant could be injured.

item.title: GM SUVs, Trucks: Roof-Rail Air Bag May Underperform
item.description: On affected vehicles, a part called the diffuser, inside the roof-rail air bag inflator, may not have been properly attached to the inflator. This means the diffuser could come apart from the inflator when the air bag deploys.

item.title: Buick Regal Front Seat Frame Weld Defect
item.description: Certain Buick Regal vehicles have a front seat frame with a lower crossbar that may not have been welded correctly, on either the driver's or passenger's seat. Seats with this kind of weld problem may not hold together as well as they should, which can affect how much protection the seat provides in a crash.

item.title: Buick Enclave, Chevy Traverse Frame Rail Crack
item.description: Some Buick Enclave and Chevrolet Traverse vehicles may have a crack in the frame rail on the right side of the engine compartment.

item.title: Buick, Chevrolet Vehicles' Air Bags May Not Deploy
item.description: On certain 2019 Buick Encore, Chevrolet Spark, Traverse, and Trax vehicles, the computer module that controls the air bags may have been left switched to a factory 'manufacturing mode' instead of being switched over to normal driving mode before the vehicle was sold. While the module is in that mode, the air bags will not deploy if the vehicle is in a crash.

item.title: Chevrolet, Buick, Cadillac, GMC Rear Brake Issue
item.description: The rear brake caliper pistons on these vehicles may not have enough of a protective coating, which can allow gas pockets to form inside them. If this happens, it can reduce how well the rear brakes perform. This affects a range of Buick, Cadillac, Chevrolet, and GMC models. To fix the problem, GM will notify owners, and dealers will bleed the vehicle's brake system. This repair is free of charge.

item.title: GM Vehicles Fuel Pump May Detach, Damage Line
item.description: General Motors is recalling a range of vehicles, including the Buick LaCrosse, Cadillac ATS, Chevrolet Colorado, Chevrolet Malibu, Chevrolet Equinox, GMC Acadia, GMC Canyon and GMC Terrain. The high pressure fuel pump, part of the fuel system, may come loose from its mounting flange while the vehicle is being driven. If the pump detaches, it could damage the nearby high pressure fuel line.

item.title: Buick Regal Rear Seat Belts May Be Misrouted
item.description: On some Buick Regal vehicles, the rear outboard seat belts may have been routed incorrectly around a bracket during manufacturing instead of the proper path. Because of this, the seat belt may not hold a passenger securely in place the way it should.
